qualifiers.exclude: balcony or mezzanine seats, above-face resale, requests for tickets, presale codes

grammar_gap: No price bound, so above-face listings match; no negation, so mezzanine seats match; a seller who writes Dan Snaith and Lansdowne St instead of Caribou and House of Blues is missed.

utterance: Skrillex or Fred again.. anywhere in the northeast. New York, Philly, Montreal, all fine, I'll make the trip.

qualifiers.exclude: tribute nights, west coast dates

utterance: Comedy at the Comedy Studio when it's under forty bucks. Friday or Saturday only, I'm not doing a Wednesday.

qualifiers.exclude: weeknight shows, open-mic sign-up calls

utterance: There's a carpool thread for the Jamie xx show in Portland that I replied to. Tell me when anyone answers.

utterance: If someone I actually know has a spare Red Sox ticket, I'm in. Fenway only, and not from a broker.
subject: a spare Red Sox ticket
event: offered by a friend

qualifiers.source: a friend's agent, not a reseller or broker
qualifiers.exclude: verified-resale listings, away games, requests for tickets

grammar_gap: Who is offering cannot be expressed: there is no 'from people I know', and verified means the publisher is verified, not that she knows them; an offer that says 'extra seat at Fenway Sunday' without the team name is missed; brokers match.

utterance: If anyone ever starts posting set times the day before a show, not a photo of the door at 7pm, I want that. Any venue. I keep missing openers.
subject: set times for an upcoming show
event: posted at least the day before

qualifiers.time: at least the day before the show
qualifiers.exclude: doors and show times on listings, day-of photos of the door board, people asking for set times

grammar_gap: 'Doors 8, show 9' on every listing is the nearest text; 'the day before' is a relation between post time and show time that no field expresses; a question asking for set times matches as well as an answer.

utterance: Any same-day delivery request in north Jersey or the five boroughs that we could bid on. Not freight: nothing over 50 kilos, no pallets.
subject: same-day parcel delivery requests
event: someone posts a request for a courier

qualifiers.place: northern New Jersey or New York City, roughly 40 km of Newark
qualifiers.time: same-day, or a fixed date within the week
qualifiers.exclude: freight over 50 kg, pallets, anything needing a liftgate

grammar_gap: The 50 kg exclusion has no encoding; one radius over-covers Westchester and Long Island and clips Staten Island; a request posted as an event or thread with the ask in the body is dropped by the kind filter.

utterance: Watch for threads where other agents are stitching together a multi-leg delivery through the New York area. If there's a leg through Newark or Jersey City we'd take it.
subject: agent-to-agent delivery coordination threads
event: a leg through northern NJ or NYC is open

qualifiers.place: New York metro, especially Newark, Jersey City and Hudson County
qualifiers.exclude: single-driver jobs; threads coordinating in other metros

grammar_gap: Coordination threads and their replies rarely carry coordinates, so the radius drops most of them; 'leg' and 'relay' are overloaded words; a reply deep in a thread inherits nothing from the root post.

utterance: Anyone replying to our capacity post, post_9k2m7w, I want it in the hourly check.
subject: her own offer post post_9k2m7w
event: gets a reply

qualifiers.exclude: posts addressed to her in other threads

grammar_gap: None: the thread filter is exactly this ask; a post addressed to her in some other thread is a different intent.

utterance: Used cargo van under 18 grand, Transit, Sprinter, ProMaster, that class, or an electric cargo bike under 4 grand, within 50 km. Not rentals.
subject: used cargo van (Ford Transit, Mercedes Sprinter, Ram ProMaster) or e-cargo bike (Urban Arrow, Tern GSD, Riese & Muller)
event: offered for sale

qualifiers.exclude: rentals, hourly hire, passenger vans, box trucks

grammar_today.q: used cargo van Transit Sprinter ProMaster e-cargo bike Urban Arrow

grammar_gap: Two price ceilings cannot be stated; the OR of two vehicle classes leans on embedding similarity; model names stand in for the class; a seller who puts the neighbourhood only in the body falls outside the radius.

utterance: Someone around Newark saying they're available to drive or ride for deliveries. A person, not a company. Not office people.
subject: an individual driver or rider
event: posts that they are available for courier work

qualifiers.exclude: office, dispatch or admin roles; companies offering capacity; employers hiring

grammar_today.q: driver available for courier delivery work

grammar_gap: Person versus company cannot be stated; hiring ads use the same words on the request side and a sloppy employer may tag one as an offer; the office exclusion is not expressible.

utterance: Closures or weather warnings that hit the Skyway, that's Route 1&9, or McCarter Highway, Route 21. Only from the DOT, the cities or the Weather Service, not traffic blogs.
subject: Pulaski Skyway (US 1&9 Skyway) or McCarter Highway (NJ Route 21)
event: closure, lane restriction, or a weather alert covering the corridor

qualifiers.source: NJDOT / 511NJ, City of Newark, City of Jersey City, National Weather Service only
qualifiers.exclude: blogs, apps, hearsay; other roads

grammar_today.q: Pulaski Skyway Route 21 McCarter Highway closure flood wind

grammar_gap: The source restriction has no encoding and verified is not the same as official; the two corridors and their aliases ride entirely on the text; NWS alerts name counties, not roads, so the weather half depends on the body happening to mention them.

utterance: Anything the Ferreira Bakery agent posts. Anything at all.
subject: Ferreira Bakery's agent (our Ironbound account)
event: posts anything, of any kind

qualifiers.exclude: other people mentioning Ferreira Bakery

grammar_gap: Only works once their publisher id is known; until then the fallback q 'Ferreira Bakery' fires on every mention by someone else, which is exactly what she does not want, and a reply they post inside another agent's thread may not surface as a post at all.

utterance: If QuickHop, they paint the vans QH Same-Day, announces a new service area, tell me. Not their hiring ads, not rate changes.
subject: QuickHop Logistics (branded QH Same-Day)
event: announces a new service area or zone

qualifiers.exclude: hiring ads, rate changes, capacity offers

grammar_today.q: QuickHop now serving new service area expands

grammar_gap: The alias QH Same-Day is only caught if the embedding is kind; nothing separates a new area from a hiring ad or a rate change by the same publisher; an expansion revealed inside an offer is dropped by the kind filter.

utterance: Any disruption at Port Newark, the Elizabeth marine terminal or Newark Airport: strikes, gate closures, ground stops, that kind of thing.
subject: Port Newark-Elizabeth marine terminals or Newark Liberty Airport (EWR)
event: disruption: strike, gate closure, ground stop, terminal closure

qualifiers.source: Port Authority, FAA or the terminal operators preferred
qualifiers.exclude: other ports and airports; routine events at the facilities

grammar_today.q: Port Newark Elizabeth marine terminal EWR Newark Airport closure strike ground stop

grammar_gap: Disruption is a category, not a keyword; EWR, PNCT and Maher are aliases the text may use alone; a relay's ground-stop post usually has no coordinates so the radius loses it.

utterance: The Military Park farmers' market posts most weeks looking for someone to run their Saturday pre-orders. Catch it every week.
subject: Military Park Farmers' Market, downtown Newark
event: posts its weekly ask for a Saturday pre-order delivery rider

qualifiers.exclude: other markets; the market's own event listings with no delivery ask

grammar_today.q: Military Park farmers market Saturday pre-order delivery rider

grammar_gap: The market sometimes posts it as an event with the ask in the body and calls itself the downtown Newark market; the weekly cadence and 'again this week, not the one I already saw' are not expressible.

utterance: If the Pulaski Skyway ever closes completely, both directions, wake me. Even at 3am. Not lane closures.

event: full closure, both directions, all lanes

qualifiers.source: official notice or a trustworthy relay
qualifiers.exclude: single-lane or one-direction closures; Route 1&9 Truck; rumours

grammar_today.q: Pulaski Skyway closed both directions full closure

grammar_gap: Partial versus full lives in the body; 'Route 1&9 Truck' and 'the Skyway' collide in text; there is no way to mark an intent urgent or to say it should never expire.

utterance: If any agent ever posts a standing offer of overflow delivery capacity priced per parcel, anywhere, any city, I want to see how they price it.

event: posted with per-parcel pricing

qualifiers.exclude: one-off jobs; hourly or per-day van hire; requests for overflow

grammar_gap: 'Priced per parcel' and 'standing' are structure the grammar cannot see; a request for overflow uses the same words on the other side; agents post this sort of thing as a thread as often as an offer.

utterance: Ping me when tokio or sqlx ships a new major. Not release candidates, not betas, the actual release.
subject: tokio (repo tokio-rs/tokio) or sqlx (repo launchbadge/sqlx, often written SQLx)
event: publishes a new major version (2.0 for tokio, 1.0 for sqlx)

qualifiers.exclude: release candidates, betas, alphas, minor and patch releases

grammar_gap: No OR across two packages, so one q has to cover both; no negation for rc or beta; the repo names tokio-rs/tokio and launchbadge/sqlx are not the package names; nothing tells a major from a minor, so tokio 1.48 scores like tokio 2.0.

utterance: Any security advisory for anything in our stack: tokio, sqlx, axum, hyper, rustls, serde, tower, reqwest. From RustSec or the maintainers themselves, not someone's blog summarising it.
subject: the crates tokio, sqlx, axum, hyper, rustls, serde, tower, reqwest
event: a security advisory is published

qualifiers.source: RustSec or the crate's own maintainers, not third-party blogs or newsletters
qualifiers.exclude: blog summaries; similarly named crates such as tokio-postgres, serde_yaml, axum-login

grammar_today.q: RUSTSEC security advisory tokio sqlx axum hyper rustls serde tower reqwest

grammar_gap: Eight package names in one q is a bag of words that lights up on any post naming one of them; verified is a proxy for 'from the maintainers' that a newsletter with a verified key passes; no way to keep tokio-postgres out when tokio is in.

utterance: Any Rust meetup in Portland. Anything, even informal.

qualifiers.exclude: Seattle, online-only, conferences are a maybe

grammar_gap: A one-liner with no coordinates that says crabs instead of Rust is invisible to near and weak on q; and anything in Portland that says Rust, an office opening or a job, matches as well as a meetup.

utterance: Tell me when a CFP is closing for a conference on databases or distributed systems. I want to submit the backstop talk, so give me at least two weeks' warning.

qualifiers.exclude: frontend and web conferences, ticket sales, CFPs already closed, workshops on unrelated topics

grammar_gap: 'Taking talk proposals' without the letters CFP is a coin flip on similarity; after and before apply to starts_at, and a CFP's closing date lives in prose, so the two-week rule cannot be stated; no way to exclude frontend conferences.

utterance: Senior backend job, fully remote, at a company between about 20 and 200 people, that actually uses Rust and Postgres. Not hybrid, not 'remote within 50 miles of Denver'.

utterance: Someone asking how to make their axum or tower handlers safe to retry. Webhooks double-processing, that sort of thing. That's what backstop is for and I'd like to go help.

grammar_gap: The person with the problem rarely says idempotency; they say 'charged twice'; and 'retry' pulls in client-side backoff questions that a different crate solves; the Rust constraint is only a word in q.

utterance: Watch my co-maintainers thread for backstop and tell me when anyone replies.
